lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: function as a rule assigning exactly one output
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: function as a rule assigning exactly one output

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 7), (4, 9)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 80 components and consumes 2 per hour. It can run for at most 15 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 80 − 2h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = 1 and a(n) = a(n − 1) − 5 for n > 1. Find a(15).
In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time reaches its highest point. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the x-intercept, giving the landing time
the y-intercept, giving the launch height
an interval of decrease
the maximum, giving the greatest height and the time it occurs

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (5, 4)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 135 components and consumes 7 per hour. It can run for at most 14 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 135 − 7h in this context?
choices: all real numbers
